name: Thin sign twist with a prescribed zero in (7/8, 1)
status: proved-rel (Hoheisel-type short-interval theorem); numerics measured to 1e9; unrefereed
statement: S = set of primes with pi_S(x) = (1/2) int_2^x t^(b-1) dt/log t + O(x^(b-eta)) (greedy floor rule); eps completely multiplicative, -1 on S, +1 elsewhere; F(s) = sum eps(n) n^-s = zeta(s)(s-b)W(s), W analytic and non-vanishing on Re s > max(b-eta, b/3). Has: complete multiplicativity, unimodular local parameters at every prime, ordinary Dirichlet series, continuation past b, one simple pole at 1, eps(p) = 1 on primes of relative density one, partial sums c x + O(x^(b+epsilon)). Lacks: periodicity modulo any ideal (hence the functional equation of every twist), Lambda >= 0. Zero: simple, at s = b, any b in (1/2, 1); translate by n^(-i tau) for b + i tau. Kills: any argument for a zero-free half-plane that uses the target only through multiplicativity, local size, continuation and the pole. First failing step of the 7/8 argument: Proposition 5.1, L-periodicity of the target weight (low estimate); same property missing at Lemmas 4.8, 8.1, 17.5.
lacks: periodicity of the coefficient sequence (functional equation in the conductor aspect of twists), Lambda >= 0
